notes: Both AI clips sit in the 'world disruption' montage after the Week One card. 01 needs picture and sound (field reporter or B-roll at an airport). 02 only needs sound: the play already lays a reporter's voice over its own dusk-street picture, so the 02 candidates are judged on the voice first; their own pictures are described in case the editor wants them. Timestamps are from YouTube auto-captions (CC pop-on captions for the NBC piece) and are accurate to roughly half a second; check the cut points against the waveform. Downloads were refused with HTTP 403 on the default client and all succeeded on the retry with --js-runtimes node --extractor-args youtube:player_client=android.

aiClips.aiLine: Airlines have suspended new bookings with reservation systems offline. Passengers are queuing for flights nobody can confirm.

candidates.name: 01-aljazeera-brussels-queues
candidates.event: Collins Aerospace MUSE check-in cyberattack, Heathrow, Brussels and Berlin, 20 September 2025
candidates.speaker: voice over B-roll
candidates.quote: Cancellations, queues, and packed departure halls filled with passengers whose flights had been delayed or grounded.
candidates.onScreenText: Lower third at 4-9 s only: EUROPEAN AIRPORTS DISRUPTED / CYBERATTACK CAUSES DELAYS AND CANCELLATIONS. Flap board at 14-17 s reads CANCELLED, DELAYED, GATE OPEN beside A3 621 ATHENS, UA 995 NEWARK. No date anywhere.
candidates.picture: Brussels Airport split-flap departures board with CANCELLED and DELAYED in yellow, then a wide shot of a packed check-in hall with roped queues. Earlier (4-9 s) Heathrow T-terminal queue with the chyron; 61-78 s Berlin BER check-in hall from above and Heathrow queues.
candidates.editPlan: Simplest: keep 14.8-23.8 (9 s, the board then the Brussels queue). For the full 8 s line with more plot, splice 4.95-9.6 'A dispiriting sight for travelers. Crowds of people at London's Heathrow airport waiting to check in but going nowhere' with 14.8-23.8; same reporter voice. If the editor wants the 'confirm' idea, 70.2-77.6 'Passengers have been urged to confirm their flight details with airlines before heading to the airport' can replace the second half; picture there is Berlin and Heathrow queues. Drop 12.2-14.8 'Similar scenes in Brussels'. The chyron is on screen only at 4-9 s and is harmless (no date).
candidates.caveats: Never says 'bookings' or 'reservation systems'; it says cancellations, queues and 'delayed or grounded'. Real Collins Aerospace incident, which the audience will recognise. The reporter (Sonia Gallego) is never on camera, so this is not a field stand-up. Reporter sign-off at 82.5-85.8 must stay out.

candidates.name: 01-cbschicago-jal-tickets
candidates.event: Japan Airlines cyberattack, 26 December 2024: ticket sales halted, flights delayed
candidates.speaker: anchor voice over B-roll
candidates.quote: Japan Airlines was briefly forced to stop selling tickets today after a cyber attack. The airline says the issues began this morning and also led to long delays for both domestic and international flights.
candidates.onScreenText: EYE ON YOUR WORLD / JAPAN AIRLINES HIT BY CYBERATTACK / AIRLINE WAS FORCED TO BRIEFLY HALT TICKET SALES AND DELAY FLIGHTS. CBS News Chicago bug, 6:12 AM clock, weather strip with day names and temperatures (no date).
candidates.picture: JAL agent in uniform and mask talking to a family at a self-service check-in kiosk; from 7 s, JAL jets on the apron at Haneda.
candidates.editPlan: Keep 2.19-11.5 as one piece. Optional: cut the single word 'briefly' (about 3.0-3.4) so it reads 'Japan Airlines was forced to stop selling tickets today after a cyber attack'; the anchor's cadence should hide it. The chyron also says BRIEFLY, so either crop the bottom 15 percent or accept it; at 480p the sub-line is small. Works as the first half of a two-clip pair with the Al Jazeera queue clip: this gives 'stopped selling tickets', that gives 'queues'.
candidates.caveats: 'Stop selling tickets' is the closest any real clip gets to 'suspended new bookings'. 'Briefly' and the 90-minute fix at 11.6-15 undercut the scale; cut before 11.5. Picture is a calm kiosk, not a crowd. Only 23 s long.

candidates.name: 01-cbsny-crowdstrike-lines
candidates.event: CrowdStrike outage, 19 July 2024: airports, hospitals and banks in the New York area
candidates.speaker: anchor voice over B-roll (then field reporter from 61 s)
candidates.quote: at the airports there were crowds and long lines as people showed up not knowing the status of their flights.
candidates.onScreenText: CBS News New York bug, 74 degrees, 11:02 PM. No chyron over the airport pictures. At 33-35 s a graphic reads MEMORIAL SLOAN KETTERING CANCER CENTER / POSTPONED PROCEDURES REQUIRING ANESTHESIA.
candidates.picture: Vertical phone video of a queue at an airline counter, then people sleeping on a terminal floor with bags. At 90-98 s: a long check-in line, a blank ARRIVALS screen reading 'No Cable Connected', travellers on the floor.
candidates.editPlan: Keep 34.4-41.3 ('at the airports ... status of their flights'), starting a beat after 'anesthesia' and before the picture leaves the hospital graphic at about 35 s; if the half-second of graphic shows, start the picture at 35.5 and let the sound lead. Optionally add 41.3-47.0 'More than 4,000 flights were either cancelled around the world or delayed'. For a second fragment in the same voice family, 91.1-99.2 'the global IT glitch meant announcements by megaphones, blank digital boards and a manual check-in system' is the field reporter (Alicia Reed) over the LaGuardia line and the dead arrivals board.
candidates.caveats: 'Not knowing the status of their flights' is 'flights nobody can confirm' almost word for word, but there is no 'bookings' half. CrowdStrike is named at 11-13 s (keep out) and the crawl never dates it. The phone video is vertical with blurred side bars.

candidates.name: 01-nbc-ba-heathrow-lines
candidates.event: British Airways global IT failure, 27 May 2017: all Heathrow and Gatwick flights cancelled
candidates.speaker: field reporter voice over B-roll (Morgan Radford, London)
candidates.quote: Bags piled high. Lines snaking through the terminal. [passenger: We've been at the airport for three hours now and we haven't made it through bag drop-off.] Passengers stranded in London and across the globe after a sudden IT failure crippled British Airways. [passenger: It's quite difficult to estimate how long we'll be here.] Forcing the airline to cancel all flights from Heathrow and Gatwick airports.
candidates.onScreenText: TRAVELERS STRANDED BY BRITISH AIRWAYS COMPUTER FAILURE (from about 10 s), NBC News / Nightly News bug. 'Welcome to Terminal 5' sign at 9 s.
candidates.picture: Passenger phone selfie in a packed Heathrow hall, crowd pushing into Terminal 5, self-service kiosks showing error screens, a packed cabin, then a high wide shot of Terminal 5 full of stranded people.
candidates.editPlan: Splice three reporter fragments and drop the two passenger soundbites: 6.8-9.3 'Bags piled high. Lines snaking through the terminal' + 13.0-18.6 'Passengers stranded in London and across the globe after a sudden IT failure crippled British Airways' + 22.5-26.5 'forcing the airline to cancel all flights from Heathrow and Gatwick airports'. About 12 s; trim the last fragment to land at 8-9 s. Hard-cut the sentence at 38.4-44 ('was not an intentional attack'). Pop-on CC captions, so the times are approximate by up to a second.
candidates.caveats: 2017 footage, SD-ish and 4:3-safe framing; the audience will not recognise it as a cyber incident. Says 'IT failure', not hack. Three-fragment splice. The passenger selfie at 6-9 s is the picture under 'bags piled high'; if that looks wrong, slide the picture from 9.5-13 (T5 crowd) under it.

aiClips.aiLine: Rolling brownouts are spreading. Utilities are rotating power between neighborhoods while crews struggle to keep the grid online.

candidates.name: 02-kpix-rotating-outages
candidates.event: California ISO Flex Alert and PG&E warning of rotating outages, June 2021 heat wave
candidates.speaker: anchor at desk, then anchor voice over B-roll
candidates.quote: the state's power grid operator says some customers might face rotating power outages this evening
candidates.onScreenText: Anchor names (Allen Martin, Elizabeth Cook), SANTA ROSA 100 RIGHT NOW, 5:59 PM, KPIX 5. From 2 s a full-frame DANGEROUS HEAT graphic with a Cal ISO demand dashboard inset.
candidates.picture: Two anchors at the desk over a Bay Bridge backdrop for the first two seconds, then a 'DANGEROUS HEAT' graphic framing B-roll of transmission towers, a substation, crows on a pole, and the Cal ISO control room.
candidates.editPlan: Sound only over the play's dusk street: keep 3.0-9.3. To reach 8 s add 21.76-25.0 'all customers are being urged to conserve power now' (same anchor, same breath). Skip 9.4-13.6 ('between seven and nine o'clock') and 28.8-31 ('strained by our dangerous heat'). Do not use the picture; the DANGEROUS HEAT frame gives away the cause.
candidates.caveats: Says 'rotating power outages', not 'rolling brownouts', and never mentions crews or neighbourhoods. The cause (heat) is in the picture, not in the kept words. 'This evening' is fine for the montage.

candidates.name: 02-cbssacramento-rotating-crews

candidates.speaker: field reporter voice over B-roll
candidates.quote: another rotating outage coming after Cal ISO issued its latest stage three emergency [...] Cal ISO is saying they ask utility companies to reduce the load to keep the power grid reliable and stable [...] as crews continued to restore power
candidates.picture: unknown (captions only); the piece opens on a couple in El Dorado Hills who lost power, with PG&E B-roll
candidates.editPlan: Three-fragment splice, same reporter: 61.9-63.9 'another rotating outage coming' + 85.1-90.4 'Cal ISO is saying they ask utility companies to reduce the load to keep the power grid reliable and stable' + 134.5-137.0 'as crews continued to restore power'. About 10 s; drop the Cal ISO clause (85.1-86.8) to land at 8. Sound only.
candidates.caveats: Captions only; picture not checked. Best vocabulary match of the set: 'rotating outage', 'keep the power grid reliable', 'crews'. Names Cal ISO and PG&E (fine). Local station audio quality unknown.

candidates.name: 02-aljazeera-kyiv-neighborhoods
candidates.event: Kyiv scheduled blackouts after Russian strikes on the grid, October 2022
candidates.speaker: voice over B-roll
candidates.quote: when darkness falls over Kyiv it falls heavy. Street lights turned off, households saving power, neighborhoods cycling through blackouts after weeks of sustained
candidates.onScreenText: Al Jazeera bug only; no chyron in the window.
candidates.picture: Night aerial of Kyiv almost entirely dark: a lit bridge and a few car headlights, then a dark boulevard with one lit intersection.
candidates.editPlan: Keep 2.75-9.15 and hard-cut before 'Russian' (9.2). Cleaner end: cut at about 8.4 after 'blackouts'. Sound over the play's dusk street fits the picture the play already has; the Al Jazeera aerial can also stand on its own as a 'city gone dark' shot. Do not continue past 9.2 (Russian strikes, then Zelensky).
candidates.caveats: Says 'Kyiv' in the first second; either accept one named city (the worm is global) or start at 4.6 'Street lights turned off, households saving power, neighborhoods cycling through blackouts' (3.8 s). No 'rotating', no 'crews'. Written VO, so the line is literary rather than newsy.

candidates.name: 02-cbs17-duke-rotating
